canonicalQuests.title: When Noon Came Bleeding
canonicalQuests.premise: A vertical wound of daylight appears above Hearthmere and begins repairing buildings while erasing the shadows of their residents.

objectives.rule: Keep the daylight wound covered without letting the cart enter complete darkness.

canonicalQuests.loreReveal: The returning light restores structures according to remembered purpose, not according to the wishes of current occupants.
canonicalQuests.dialogueThesis: A miracle can be accurate and still be wrong.

authorshipProof.setpiece: A mobile shade cart circles a vertical noon wound while repaired houses shed their occupants' shadows.
authorshipProof.failureTransformation: Losing cover does not reset the escort; it permanently assigns the exposed resident a Synod purity mark.
authorshipProof.dialogueConstraint: Nima refuses every sentence containing the word restored until the player names what restoration removed.
authorshipProof.persistentWorldChange: Hearthmere keeps either rebuilt facades, a shadow-refuge district, or a shared Dunmire noon route.
authorshipProof.forbiddenSubstitution: Cannot be reskinned as a cargo escort because cover position rewrites named residents and buildings.

canonicalQuests.title: The Saint Cast Two Shadows
canonicalQuests.premise: Vespera's second shadow commits acts of rescue she publicly condemns and executions she swears she never ordered.

objectives.rule: Every question may be asked to only one version.

canonicalQuests.loreReveal: A Synod saint is a mortal continuity edited into a law of light, not a heavenly visitor.
canonicalQuests.dialogueThesis: A divided self may be more honest than a unified saint.

authorshipProof.setpiece: The player reconstructs one gesture from two incompatible shadow angles while each half rescues a different witness.
authorshipProof.failureTransformation: A misattributed act becomes binding testimony for the wrong Vespera rather than restarting the interrogation.
authorshipProof.dialogueConstraint: Ilar speaks only about deeds seen in shadow and physically turns away from claims made in direct light.
authorshipProof.persistentWorldChange: The saint remains unified, separates into two legal persons, or grants the shadow supervised asylum.
authorshipProof.forbiddenSubstitution: Cannot become an ordinary impostor mystery; both actors are authentic continuations of one coerced sainthood.

canonicalQuests.title: The Bell That Forgot You
canonicalQuests.premise: Halix restores natural time to three villages, but each toll deletes one relationship from the player's social history.

objectives.rule: Choose which bond the next toll may consume.

canonicalQuests.loreReveal: Halix's noon is powered by remembered social order; time returns by consuming relationships that prove change occurred.
canonicalQuests.dialogueThesis: A calendar without anyone who remembers you is another kind of death.

authorshipProof.setpiece: A repaired bell note moves through town as visible noon geometry while names disappear from doors in its wake.
authorshipProof.failureTransformation: Every mistimed bell strike restores one civic routine but severs the relationship that taught it.
authorshipProof.dialogueConstraint: Oren can answer only with dates until another character supplies the name attached to each date.
authorshipProof.persistentWorldChange: The district receives natural time, relational memory, or an unstable alternating calendar.
authorshipProof.forbiddenSubstitution: Cannot be reduced to a rhythm puzzle because each beat trades a documented relationship for physical repair.

canonicalQuests.title: The Door in Mother's Rib
canonicalQuests.premise: A refugee village hidden inside Mother Nacre has remained safe for centuries and now wants the door opened despite the lethal passage of time outside.

objectives.rule: Residents receive different evidence depending on which organs are repaired.

canonicalQuests.loreReveal: The Charnel Night began as shelters built from bodies when ordinary architecture stopped surviving the dark.
canonicalQuests.dialogueThesis: Protection without an exit is a kinder prison, not a home.

authorshipProof.setpiece: A centuries-old village votes inside a rib cage while the player's route through living arteries changes which evidence reaches each ward.
authorshipProof.failureTransformation: A blocked artery does not end the vote; it isolates a neighborhood and makes its uninformed ballot legally decisive.
authorshipProof.dialogueConstraint: Ilyen alternates a child's present tense with an elder's outside chronology and never reconciles them for the player.
authorshipProof.persistentWorldChange: The sanctuary opens, becomes consensual and mobile, or remains closed under an explicit act of captivity.
authorshipProof.forbiddenSubstitution: Cannot become a prison-break template because the prison is also a protective body and a self-governing settlement.

canonicalQuests.title: Parliament of One Mouth
canonicalQuests.premise: Thirteen voices negotiate one treaty, but one has never consented to being part of the Prince.
canonicalQuests.loreReveal: One voice inside the Prince predates the dimming and can name the law that separated light from darkness.
canonicalQuests.dialogueThesis: Perfect representation is still violence if the represented cannot leave.

authorshipProof.setpiece: Thirteen anatomical throats conduct a treaty in a circular cadence whose single silence carries a fourteenth political position.
authorshipProof.failureTransformation: Misidentifying a voice transfers its treaty obligation to another throat instead of cancelling negotiation.
authorshipProof.dialogueConstraint: Sava records consent without paraphrase and challenges any answer that collapses two voices into a group noun.
authorshipProof.persistentWorldChange: The Prince becomes a ratified polity, releases the stolen speakers, or gives the sun-voice a casting vote.
authorshipProof.forbiddenSubstitution: Cannot be reskinned as a council dialogue because representation and captivity share the same thirteen bodies.

canonicalQuests.title: The Archive of Open Wounds
canonicalQuests.premise: Keth offers proof that mortals consented to dismantling the sun, but the record can be read only by assigning its original pain to living witnesses.

objectives.rule: No witness can carry two injuries and every unassigned wound redacts part of the truth.

canonicalQuests.loreReveal: The old world dismantled its sun to stop a divine empire from using daylight as compulsory truth.
canonicalQuests.dialogueThesis: A painless history is usually the victor's preferred injury.

authorshipProof.setpiece: Four hinged wound margins replay mutually incomplete bas-relief histories only while four different witnesses carry their pain.
authorshipProof.failureTransformation: An unassigned margin redacts one causal link and produces a coherent but politically dangerous false history.
authorshipProof.dialogueConstraint: Mira states where each fact hurts before describing what it proves, and will not call suffering evidence without a bearer.
authorshipProof.persistentWorldChange: The dismantling record becomes public, partial, or privately embodied by the player.
authorshipProof.forbiddenSubstitution: Cannot become a collectible-lore quest because reading is an allocation of present harm with named consent.

canonicalQuests.title: Mercy Has a Mouth
canonicalQuests.premise: The only safe route to the Synod's dawn engine passes through the restrained Maw, which asks the party to trust that it can carry them without feeding.

objectives.rule: Each light used for navigation increases hunger; each extinguished light hides one companion.

canonicalQuests.loreReveal: The Maw holds the dark half of the First Light and may be a necessary organ of any survivable sun.
canonicalQuests.dialogueThesis: Trust is not certainty that hunger vanished; it is a negotiated risk with teeth.

authorshipProof.setpiece: Party members navigate one unconsumed path inside a sentient predator while every lamp simultaneously reveals a route and increases hunger.
authorshipProof.failureTransformation: A hidden companion is not teleported back; the Maw must choose whether to surrender a tempting memory to return them.
authorshipProof.dialogueConstraint: Fenn counts teeth only after acts of mercy and refuses to treat a promise as evidence before the count changes.
authorshipProof.persistentWorldChange: The Maw proves restraint, is fed a chosen memory, or carries a permanent emergency wound cut by the party.
authorshipProof.forbiddenSubstitution: Cannot become a dungeon traversal because the dungeon is a negotiating ally whose appetite is altered by navigation.

canonicalQuests.title: The Engine With an Off-Switch
canonicalQuests.premise: Tor can add mortality to the dawn engine, but only by making its shutdown depend on one fallible person's continued life.
canonicalQuests.loreReveal: Restoration is an engineered process with owners and failure modes, not an inevitable prophecy.
canonicalQuests.dialogueThesis: A god with an off-switch is a machine; a machine without one is a god by negligence.

authorshipProof.setpiece: Three miniature dawn disasters run concurrently while the player physically rewires who can halt each beneficial catastrophe.
authorshipProof.failureTransformation: A failed stress test survives as a permanent known fault that one settlement must knowingly inherit.
authorshipProof.dialogueConstraint: Pella describes only prior failures; every proposal must be phrased as the specific death it is willing to risk repeating.
authorshipProof.persistentWorldChange: Shutdown authority belongs to the player, a distributed settlement veto, or no mortal actor.
authorshipProof.forbiddenSubstitution: Cannot be a crafting recipe because governance ownership, not component quality, is the mechanical output.

canonicalQuests.title: A Sun Small Enough
canonicalQuests.premise: All factions converge on the final crucible, where the player must define which laws the next sun possesses and which beings it is allowed to judge.

objectives.rule: Choose a limited set of incompatible light laws earned by prior outcomes.

canonicalQuests.loreReveal: The next age is not selected by morality points; it is constituted from every cost the player previously made someone else carry.
canonicalQuests.dialogueThesis: Salvation becomes tyranny at the exact boundary where it stops asking who survives it.

authorshipProof.setpiece: Incompatible laws of warmth, truth, growth, and admission orbit a hand-sized crucible while prior quest consequences speak as witnesses.
authorshipProof.failureTransformation: An unstable law is not rejected; it enters the new cosmology with a named exception inherited from the campaign ledger.
authorshipProof.dialogueConstraint: Solenne answers each faction in the vocabulary of the sky that would reject her and never endorses a universal solution.
authorshipProof.persistentWorldChange: The campaign constitutes a mortal dawn, full restoration, negotiated dusk, or deliberate continuation of the Late World.
authorshipProof.forbiddenSubstitution: Cannot become a colored-ending choice because every available law and exception is earned from persistent prior state.

canonicalQuests.title: The Disease Called Grief
canonicalQuests.premise: Vael can cure a widower's disabling grief, but the grief is the last surviving evidence that his spouse existed.
canonicalQuests.loreReveal: The Synod's cleanest miracles often destroy the evidence needed to judge whether the cure was merciful.
canonicalQuests.dialogueThesis: Pain is not sacred, but neither is relief innocent.

authorshipProof.setpiece: Four layers of one widower's grief appear as surgical threads linking bodily function to evidence of an erased spouse.
authorshipProof.failureTransformation: Cutting a thread early cures one symptom while making its attached memory permanently unverifiable.
authorshipProof.dialogueConstraint: Davren never supplies his wife's name; the player must discuss her through effects that survive without inventing an idealized portrait.
authorshipProof.persistentWorldChange: Grief remains with restored function, grief and evidence vanish, or Vael becomes a co-bearer of the memory.
authorshipProof.forbiddenSubstitution: Cannot be a cure-or-no-cure dialogue because diagnosis physically separates function, pain, testimony, and identity.

canonicalQuests.title: Seven Lamps for Six Streets
canonicalQuests.premise: A seventh municipal lamp illuminates a street absent from every map and populated by people omitted from Hearthmere's ration count.
canonicalQuests.loreReveal: The League's founding arithmetic already excludes people it claims to protect.
canonicalQuests.dialogueThesis: A place can be saved from danger by the same omission that starves it.

authorshipProof.setpiece: Seven different lamps reveal six budgeted streets and one moving address that exists only between maintenance rounds.
authorshipProof.failureTransformation: An extinguished lamp relocates Nullstreet and strands a specific household in another jurisdiction rather than resetting the route.
authorshipProof.dialogueConstraint: Roa uses addresses as names and will not describe a person without stating where the ledger refuses to place them.
authorshipProof.persistentWorldChange: Nullstreet becomes registered and taxable, remains hidden and ration-poor, or joins the Unwritten Roads.
authorshipProof.forbiddenSubstitution: Cannot be a lamp-lighting checklist because each lamp changes civic visibility, ration entitlement, and physical geography.

canonicalQuests.title: The Hospice Grows a Heart
canonicalQuests.premise: The neutral hospice develops a living heart and begins rearranging beds according to Calve's unconscious judgments of whose life is most useful.
canonicalQuests.loreReveal: Neutral systems inherit moral choices even when no one writes those choices down.
canonicalQuests.dialogueThesis: Triage is a story about worth disguised as a queue.

authorshipProof.setpiece: A newly grown hospice heart rolls six occupied beds through living corridors according to an unspoken hierarchy of usefulness.
authorshipProof.failureTransformation: A patient displaced from care changes the heart's learned bias and later becomes the test case for the next edit.
authorshipProof.dialogueConstraint: Bek discusses policy only through the bed currently denied to someone else and refuses abstract statistics.
authorshipProof.persistentWorldChange: Triage becomes random, biased but appealable, or manual after the living heart is destroyed.
authorshipProof.forbiddenSubstitution: Cannot become a healer fetch quest because the antagonist is an adaptive priority rule inherited from a trusted caregiver.
